To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the coarse-grained MHD equations contain both a subsale stress and a subsale EMF, and 2) the subscale nonlinearities can persist to arbitrarily high Reynolds numbers, thus providing a mechanism for the nonlinear transfer of invariants across scales.

the effective equations derived by coarse-graining incompressible magnetofluiddynamics (i) have a subscale stress $\tau_{ij}$ and subscale EMFs $\xi_{i}$ that arise from the nonlinear interaction of eliminated velocity and magnetic fields, (ii) the subscale stress and EMFs can transfer energy and helicity between scales, and (iii) this inter-scale cascade of energy and helicity is not prohibited, even for smooth velocity and magnetic fields.
the coarse-graining of MHD turbulence is a nontrivial problem that is not solved by the usual closure approximations and requires further research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of a general framework for the coarse-graining of MHD fluids, and with the application of the resulting effective equations to MHD turbulence.
the derivation of effective equations for coarse-grained MHD fluids and their applications to the study of MHD turbulence.
the derivation of effective equations of motion and the analysis of the nonlinear cascade processes in coarse-grained MHD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the forward cascades of energy and cross helicity are possible and the forward cascade of the magnetic helicity is forbidden in the incompressible MHD turbulence.
the coarse-grained incompressibility of MHD turbulence allows for a cascade of energy and of cross-helicity, but not of magnetic helicity.
the coarse-grained MHD turbulence is not in a steady state and is not self-similar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear cascade of MHD turbulence can occur in both the energy and cross-helical cascades, but the magnetic helicity cascade can only occur in a weak form.

in the case that both velocity and magnetic fields have roughness exponents $\zeta$ satisfying $\zeta<2$, the nonlinear cascade of invariants is possible and the MHD turbulent cascade is not a simple Richardson cascade of energy and magnetic energy.
the coarse-graining methodology is a powerful tool for analyzing the dynamics of incompressible fluids and plasmas, and for deriving rigorous constraints on the phenomenology of turbulence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effective equations derived from coarse-graining can be used to analyze the turbulent cascade in terms of work, dissipation and helicity.
the effective dissipation of invariances in MHD turbulence is dominated by nonlinear inter-scale transfer, rather than direct dissipation by microscopic mechanisms.

the nonlinear transfer of invariants is an important mechanism for energy dissipation in MHD turbulence, and can persist to asymptotically low scales, provided that the velocity and/or magnetic field are sufficiently rough.
